sections.content:
This master pushed me to reflect more seriously than I had planned. Initially, I considered it annoying, but it became one of the most valuable parts, confronting me with questions I would otherwise have postponed indefinitely.

It taught me that this master helped me develop alot personally, but professionally, it showed me that the work I actually want to be doing is not only the design side, but the technical core underneath: programming, electronics, hardware and software. That is the part that pulled me in across every project. I could chase it from a design role, and the human-centered view I have built here is real and worth contributing, but I would always be reaching for the engineering from the outside.

So I'm being deliberate, my next step is a master's in Robotics in Twente, the degree that matches what I want day-to-day, what I kept gravitating toward. Looking further ahead, I want to move toward the space sector, ESA or commercial.

A direction I'd wanted for a long time and wasn't decisive enough to chase until this program forced me to sit with the question. The design vision doesn't disappear, it stays something I can act on from a design role. None of this makes the past two years a detour. That clarity is, in a slightly ironic way, exactly what this master's taught me to find.
